lines.text: faced. Another big challenge was the condition of the ground below the water. The
underwater clay was the soft clay also known as alluvial clay, which holds 70% of water.
To deal with this, engineers used sand drains. Constructing a sea wall around the sand
drain was another challenge, else the chances of the airport collapsing were quite high.
However, engineers and technicians made the impossible possible and airport was
operational in 1994. When designed and built, the airport had the longest terminal in
the world which was around 1.7 km long.
This amazing island airport is connected to the mainland with a 3.75 km bridge known
as the 'Kansai International Airport Access Bridge.'
Since the airport is built on artificial islands, the chances of its sinking are quite high.
Therefore, it remains under the scrutiny of engineers and local authorities.
